title: asks before a quit during a layout, which only the report from the page shows
why: The layout term dropped: a quit during a layout, which is not in flight in the main process between its steps, goes ahead unasked and the layout is lost.

title: asks before a close during an export too, on macOS as everywhere
why: The close's export term dropped, which is the exception the approach first decided gave macOS, in the only form a rule with no platform can hold it: a window closed during an export closes unasked.

title: never asks about a quit of the app itself
why: The bypass for the app's own quits dropped: the crash box's Quit, or the quit that follows the window, is held behind a question nobody chose to be asked.

title: does not ask when the renderer is gone, so a person can always quit
why: The renderer-gone bypass dropped: a quit is held for a question no page is there to show, and the app cannot be quit.

title: does not ask when the renderer is unresponsive
why: The unresponsive bypass dropped: a quit is held for a question sent to a page that is not answering.

title: goes ahead with nothing running, as every quit and close did before
why: The nothing-running term dropped: every quit and every close is held behind a question about no run.

title: names the projects in the order their runs started, whichever kind each is
why: The runs left in the order they were handed in: the sentence names the exports' projects first, whenever each run started.

find: for (const run of runs) if (!named.has(run.project)) named.set(run.project, run.name)
replace: for (const run of runs) named.set(`${run.project} ${run.started}`, run.name)
title: names a project once, however many of its runs are going
why: Every run named, not every project: a project with an export and a layout is said twice in one sentence.

find: if (facts.open !== null) return facts.open < QUESTION_MIN_AGE_MS ? HOLD : GO_AHEAD
title: lets a second quit go ahead once the question has been open a second: it is an answer
why: The second-quit rule dropped: a quit made while the question is open is asked about again, so the question can never be answered by quitting.

find: if (facts.open !== null) return facts.open < QUESTION_MIN_AGE_MS ? HOLD : GO_AHEAD
title: lets a second quit go ahead once the question has been open a second: it is an answer
why: A second quit held however old the question is: with a dialog that cannot be answered, the app can never be quit.

find: if (facts.open !== null) return facts.open < QUESTION_MIN_AGE_MS ? HOLD : GO_AHEAD
title: holds a second quit that comes before the question could have been read
why: The question's age not looked at: the repeat of a held shortcut, or the second click of a double click, answers the question it has only just asked, and the run is thrown away unread.

find: if (facts.open !== null) return facts.open < QUESTION_MIN_AGE_MS ? HOLD : GO_AHEAD
replace: if (facts.open !== null) return facts.open <= QUESTION_MIN_AGE_MS ? HOLD : GO_AHEAD
title: lets a second quit go ahead once the question has been open a second: it is an answer
why: The boundary moved: a quit made exactly a second after the question is held, where the rule says it goes ahead.

title: does not hold a second quit for a page that can no longer show the question
why: A second quit held for a page that has gone or stopped answering: for a second after a question it cannot show, the app cannot be quit.
